new: Acts 29:2 — *certain of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), about the time of the Assyrian captivity, had escaped by sea to "the isles afar off,"* This is the manuscript's reason for Paul's journey to Spain and Britain, following the lost sheep of Matthew 10:6 to where they were scattered.

Acts 29:3 — *Yahuah (Lord) commanded the gospel to be preached far hence to the Gentiles, and to the lost sheep of the House of Yashar'el (Israel).* The manuscript carries the commission of Matthew 10:6 and Matthew 15:24 out to the far places where the scattered flock was driven.

Acts 29:13 — *certain of the Druids came unto Paul privately, and showed by their rites and ceremonies they were descended from the Yahudim (Jews) which escaped from bondage in the land of Egypt.* The manuscript has Paul finding the scattered children in Britain, where Matthew 10:23 says the cities of Yashar'el (Israel) are not yet fully gone over.

Matthew 15:24 — *But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* Yahusha (Jesus) names the same flock that Acts 29:3 says Yahuah (the Lord) commanded the gospel to be preached to, "the lost sheep of the House of Yashar'el (Israel)."

Acts 9:15 — *But Yahusha (Lord) said unto him, Go thy way: for he is a chosen vessel unto me, to bear my name before the Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* Yahusha (Jesus) chose Paul to bear his name before the Gentiles, kings, and the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and the Acts 29:4 words "he testified boldly of Yahusha (Jesus) before the tribunes and among the people" show that name being borne.

Matthew 7:2 — *For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged: and with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you again.* Clement quotes this measure-for-measure word of the Master almost verbatim to summon the Corinthians to forbearance (1 Clement 1:13).
Matthew 5:7 — *Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.* The beatitude is the very 'have mercy, that ye may receive mercy' Clement cites as the Master's command (1 Clement 1:13).

Psalms 19:1 — *The heavens declare the glory of Elohim (God); and the firmament sheweth his handywork.* Clement's ordered, obedient heavens echo this psalm of the firmament proclaiming its Maker (1 Clement 1:20).
Psalms 19:2 — *Day unto day uttereth speech, and night unto night sheweth knowledge.* Clement's day and night, which keep the course given them, are this psalm's unceasing witness (1 Clement 1:20).

Job 38:7 — *When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of Elohim (God) shouted for joy?* The harmony of the dancing stars Clement describes is the founded-creation order of Job's whirlwind speech (1 Clement 1:20).

1 Corinthians 15:36 — *Thou fool, that which thou sowest is not quickened, except it die.* Paul's seed that is not quickened unless it dies is the picture Clement draws of the sower: the seeds fall into the earth dry and bare and decay, and then the Master's providence raises them up and they bear fruit (1 Clement 1:24).

Numbers 17:8 — *And it came to pass, that on the morrow Moses went into the tabernacle of witness; and, behold, the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi was budded, and brought forth buds, and bloomed blossoms, and yielded almonds.* Clement recounts this Torah sign of the budding rod to prove that Elohim, not man, appoints the priestly order (1 Clement 1:43).

Hebrews 5:4 — *And no man taketh this honour unto himself, but he that is called of Elohim (God), as was Aaron.* Hebrews and Clement share the rule that priestly honour is not self-seized but divinely called, the very lesson of Aaron's rod (1 Clement 1:43).

1 Corinthians 13:4 — *Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up.* Clement's "is long-suffering in all things. There is nothing coarse, nothing arrogant in love" is Paul's love chapter, the cure he offers the envious Corinthians (1 Clement 1:49).

Deuteronomy 30:15 — *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil;* the Didache's two ways, "one of life and one of death," simply re-utter the choice Moses set before Yashar'el (Israel) (Didache 1:1).

Leviticus 19:18 — *Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am Yahuah (LORD).* The Didache's "thou shalt not cherish a grudge" and its "{and others thou shalt love} more than thy life" echo this verse (Didache 1:2).

Deuteronomy 4:2 — *Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall ye diminish ought from it, that ye may keep the commandments of Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) which I command you.* The Didache's "neither adding to them nor taking away from them" is Moses' own guard upon the commandments (Didache 1:4).

1 Thessalonians 4:16 — *For Yahusha (Lord) himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of Elohim (God): and the dead in Messiah (Christ) shall rise first:* the trumpet and resurrection the Didache lists as signs of the end are Paul's same hope.

2 Peter 3:9 — *Yahuah (Lord) is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.* The "time" and the "One that receiveth us" in 2 Clement 1:16 are the longsuffering of Yahuah (the Lord) holding the door open: Clement says "seeing that we have time" and "while we have still One that receiveth us."

Jeremiah 18:4 — *And the vessel that he made of clay was marred in the hand of the potter: so he made it again another vessel, as seemed good to the potter to make it.* The homilist's twisted-then-reshaped vessel in 2 Clement 1:8 is Jeremiah's parable verbatim.

Jeremiah 18:6 — *O house of Yashar'el (Israel), cannot I do with you as this potter? saith Yahuah (LORD). Behold, as the clay is in the potter’s hand, so are ye in mine hand, O house of Yashar'el (Israel).* Clement's "we are clay under the craftsman's hand" (2 Clement 1:8) is the word of Yahuah (the LORD) to the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and the reshaping mercy of the potter stands.

Isaiah 64:8 — *But now, O Yahuah (LORD), thou art our father; we are the clay, and thou our potter; and we all are the work of thy hand.* The homily's plea to be remade before the oven echoes Isaiah's confession of the Father as potter.

1 Corinthians 15:44 — *It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. There is a natural body, and there is a spiritual body.* Clement speaks of those who have "kept the flesh pure" (2 Clement 1:8) and then bids them "guard the flesh as a temple of Elohim (God)" (2 Clement 1:9), because it rises again; Sha'ul's body raised spiritual shows the flesh raised, not abolished.

Malachi 4:1 — *For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble: and the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), that it shall leave them neither root nor branch.* The day of judgment that Clement says "cometh even now as a burning oven" (2 Clement 1:16) is the day Malachi says "shall burn as an oven."

Matthew 7:21 — *Not every one that saith unto me, Adonai (Lord), Adonai (Lord), shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.* The warning that calling Him 'Lord' will not save in 2 Clement 1:4 is the Master's own word, quoted nearly verbatim.

1 John 2:17 — *And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of Elohim (God) abideth for ever.* Clement's "let us confess Him in our works" and "he that doeth righteousness" (2 Clement 1:4) are Yochanan's doer of the will of Elohim (God) who abides.

Ezekiel 14:20 — *Though Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, as I live, saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD), they shall deliver neither son nor daughter; they shall but deliver their own souls by their righteousness.* The warning that even the righteous cannot deliver their children (2 Clement 1:6) is Ezekiel's word that each delivers but his own soul.

Isaiah 66:18 — *For I know their works and their thoughts: it shall come, that I will gather all nations and tongues; and they shall come, and see my glory.* The homilist's quoted promise 'I come to gather together all the nations, tribes, and languages' at 2 Clement 1:17 is Isaiah's ingathering of all nations and tongues.

1 John 4:2 — *Hereby know ye the Spirit of Elohim (God): Every spirit that confesseth that Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) is come in the flesh is of Elohim (God):* John gives the very test of true confession that Ignatius wields in Ignatius to the Ephesians 1:18 against those who deny the Messiah's flesh.

Matthew 1:23 — *Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, Elohim (God) with us.* Matthew records the fulfilment of the virgin-birth Ignatius confesses in Ignatius to the Ephesians 1:18.

Isaiah 7:14 — *Therefore Yahuah (Lord) himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.* The virgin-conception Ignatius affirms in Ignatius to the Ephesians 1:18 was promised by the prophet centuries before.

2 Timothy 2:8 — *Remember that Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) of the seed of David was raised from the dead according to my gospel:* matches Ignatius to the Ephesians 1:20, who calls him the one who after the flesh was of David's race and points to his passion and resurrection.

Genesis 1:14 — *And Elohim (God) said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years:* the lights were ordained for signs from creation, and one such sign heralded the King in Ignatius to the Ephesians 1:19.

Numbers 24:17 — *I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Yashar'el (Israel), and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth.* Balaam's Star out of Jacob is the ancient prophecy behind the outshining star of Ignatius to the Ephesians 1:19.

Matthew 2:9 — *When they had heard the king, they departed; and, lo, the star, which they saw in the east, went before them, till it came and stood over where the young child was.* Matthew confirms the heavenly sign at the nativity that Ignatius exalts in Ignatius to the Ephesians 1:19.

Matthew 2:2 — *Saying, Where is he that is born King of the Yahudim (Jews)? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him.* The star Ignatius describes in Ignatius to the Ephesians 1:19 is the very star the magi followed to the newborn King.

Matthew 18:20 — *For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.* The indwelling Ignatius desires in Ignatius to the Ephesians 1:15, that we be His temples, is the Messiah's own promise to the gathered.

Ephesians 2:22 — *In whom ye also are builded together for an habitation of Elohim (God) through the Spirit.* The Ephesians being built together into a habitation of Elohim (God) is what Ignatius means when he calls them "stones of a temple, which were prepared beforehand for a building of Elohim (God) the Father" (Ignatius to the Ephesians 1:9).

Ephesians 2:21 — *In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in Yahusha (Lord):* Paul's holy temple of living stones is the image Ignatius takes up in Ignatius to the Ephesians 1:9 for the Ephesians built into Elohim's house.

Ephesians 4:6 — *One Elohim (God) and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all.* The one Father unto whom Ignatius would have them sing with one voice in Ignatius to the Ephesians 1:4.
Ephesians 4:5 — *One Adonai (Lord), one faith, one baptism,* echoes Ignatius's call in Ignatius to the Ephesians 1:20 to assemble in one faith and one Messiah.

Ephesians 4:4 — *There is one body, and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling;* the one body and one hope is the harmonious unity Ignatius seeks in Ignatius to the Ephesians 1:5.

Ephesians 4:3 — *Endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.* Paul's charge to keep the Spirit's unity is the very concord Ignatius urges on the Ephesians in Ignatius to the Ephesians 1:4.

Proverbs 3:34 — *Surely he scorneth the scorners: but he giveth grace unto the lowly.* The Tanakh root of the proverb Ignatius quotes in Ignatius to the Ephesians 1:5, carried forward by James and Peter.

1 Peter 5:5 — *Likewise, ye younger, submit yourselves unto the elder. Yea, all of you be subject one to another, and be clothed with humility: for Elohim (God) resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble.* Peter joins submission to elders with the same word Ignatius cites in Ignatius to the Ephesians 1:5 against the proud who separate.

James 4:6 — *But he giveth more grace. Wherefore he saith, Elohim (God) resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble.* The exact saying Ignatius quotes as Scripture in Ignatius to the Ephesians 1:5 stands written in James.

Exodus 15:26 — *And said, If thou wilt diligently hearken to the voice of Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), and wilt do that which is right in his sight, and wilt give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of these diseases upon thee, which I have brought upon the Egyptians: for I am Yahuah Rapha (the LORD that healeth thee).* Yahuah (the LORD) who heals, and who binds his healing to hearkening to his commandments, is the one physician of flesh and spirit named in Ignatius to the Ephesians 1:7.

Matthew 9:12 — *But when Yahusha (Jesus) heard that, he said unto them, They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.* The Messiah calls himself the physician of the sick, the one only physician Ignatius confesses in Ignatius to the Ephesians 1:7.

1 Corinthians 5:8 — *Therefore let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, neither with the leaven of malice and wickedness; but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.* Paul's leaven figure purges malice while keeping the feast — the leaven of Ignatius to the Magnesians 1:10 is the leaven of wickedness, not the appointed times themselves.

Mark 2:28 — *Therefore the Son of Adam is Adonai (Lord) also of the sabbath.* The Messiah is the sabbath's Lord, not its abolisher — the truth that corrects the antinomian turn of Ignatius to the Magnesians 1:9.

Matthew 5:17 — *Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.* Ignatius to the Magnesians 1:9 says that if we "live after the manner of Judaism, we avow that we have not received grace"; beside that line stands the word of Yahusha (Jesus) himself, who did not come to destroy the law or the prophets.

2 Peter 2:1 — *But there were false prophets also among the people, even as there shall be false teachers among you, who privily shall bring in damnable heresies, even denying Yahusha (Lord) that bought them, and bring upon themselves swift destruction.* Peter's false teachers who "privily shall bring in damnable heresies" are the men Ignatius says "do even mingle poison with Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ), imposing upon others by a show of honesty, like persons administering a deadly drug with honied wine" (Ignatius to the Trallians 1:6).
Ephesians 4:5 — *One Adonai (Lord), one faith, one baptism,* The single faith and Lord is the unity Ignatius guards against the schismatic poison of heresy.

Ephesians 4:4 — *There is one body, and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling.* Paul's one body and one Spirit stand behind Ignatius's call to be obedient to the presbytery "as to the Apostles of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) our hope" (Ignatius to the Trallians 1:2).

Romans 1:3 — *Concerning his Son Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh.* Ignatius's "the flesh of Messiah (Christ) who was of the seed of David" (Ignatius to the Romans 1:7) says what Sha'ul says in the opening of Romans, that the Son was made of the seed of David according to the flesh.

Romans 6:5 — *For if we have been planted together in the likeness of his death, we shall be also in the likeness of his resurrection.* Ignatius's "I shall rise free in Him" (Ignatius to the Romans 1:4) looks to the same hope Sha'ul sets out, that those planted together in the likeness of his death will be in the likeness of his resurrection.
Ephesians 4:5 — *One Adonai (Lord), one faith, one baptism,* The oneness Ignatius presses in the eucharist stands on the one Yahuah and one faith confessed before him.

1 Corinthians 10:17 — *For we being many are one bread, and one body: for we are all partakers of that one bread.* The one flesh and one altar of Ignatius to the Philadelphians 1:4 is the one bread, one body of the many made one.

Isaiah 53:5 — *But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.* Ignatius speaks of "His most blessed passion" (Ignatius to the Smyrnaeans 1:1), foretold by the prophet.

Romans 1:3 — *Concerning his Son Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;* Ignatius's "truly of the race of David according to the flesh" (Ignatius to the Smyrnaeans 1:1) is Paul's very confession against any who deny the real incarnation.

1 John 1:1 — *That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, which we have looked upon, and our hands have handled, of the Word of life;* John's hands-have-handled witness undergirds Ignatius's "they touched Him" in Ignatius to the Smyrnaeans 1:3.

Acts 10:41 — *Not to all the people, but unto witnesses chosen before of Elohim (God), even to us, who did eat and drink with him after he rose from the dead.* Peter names the very eating-and-drinking with the risen Lord that Ignatius rehearses in Ignatius to the Smyrnaeans 1:3.

Luke 24:43 — *And he took it, and did eat before them.* Ignatius writes that "after His resurrection He [both] ate with them and drank with them as one in the flesh" (Ignatius to the Smyrnaeans 1:3), the same meal Luke sets down.

Luke 24:39 — *Behold my hands and my feet, that it is I myself: handle me, and see; for a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as ye see me have.* Ignatius's "Lay hold and handle me, and see that I am not a demon without body" (Ignatius to the Smyrnaeans 1:3) quotes the risen Messiah's own proof of flesh.

Acts 10:40 — *Him Elohim (God) raised up the third day, and shewed him openly;* "He raised Himself truly" (Ignatius to the Smyrnaeans 1:2) and was shewn openly, the bodily resurrection over against every docetic semblance.

Isaiah 53:8 — *He was taken from prison and from judgment: and who shall declare his generation? for he was cut off out of the land of the living: for the transgression of my people was he stricken.* The true death Ignatius defends in Ignatius to the Smyrnaeans 1:2 was foretold as a real cutting-off from the land of the living.

Isaiah 53:7 — *He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth: he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth.* Ignatius's "He suffered truly" (Ignatius to the Smyrnaeans 1:2) is the lamb's real affliction the prophet saw, not semblance.

Isaiah 53:5 — *But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.* Ignatius bids them "give heed to the Prophets, and especially to the Gospel, wherein the passion is shown unto us" (Ignatius to the Smyrnaeans 1:7), and this oracle of Isaiah, wounded for our transgressions, is among the Prophets he points to.

Malachi 4:4 — *Remember ye the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Yashar'el (Israel), with the statutes and judgments.* The prophets' closing charge is the very "law of Moses" Ignatius says the unbelievers refused (Ignatius to the Smyrnaeans 1:5).

Matthew 5:18 — *For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.* The law of Moses Ignatius commends in Ignatius to the Smyrnaeans 1:5 endures to the last jot and tittle.

Matthew 5:17 — *Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.* When Ignatius faults the deniers for spurning "the law of Moses" (Ignatius to the Smyrnaeans 1:5), he stands with the Messiah who came to fulfil, not destroy, the Torah.

1 Corinthians 11:26 — *For as often as ye eat this bread, and drink this cup, ye do shew the death of Yahusha (the Lord) till he come.* The one valid love-feast Ignatius guards in Ignatius to the Smyrnaeans 1:8 shews forth the very death-and-return the docetists denied.

1 Corinthians 11:24 — *And when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me.* The bread that is His broken body grounds Ignatius's claim in Ignatius to the Smyrnaeans 1:6 that the eucharist is the flesh that suffered for our sins.

1 Corinthians 11:23 — *For I have received of Yahusha (the Lord) that which also I delivered unto you, That Yahusha (the Lord Jesus) the same night in which he was betrayed took bread:* Ignatius's eucharist that is "the flesh of our Saviour" (Ignatius to the Smyrnaeans 1:6) is the supper Paul received and delivered.

1 Peter 5:2 — *Feed the flock of Elohim (God) which is among you, taking the oversight thereof, not by constraint, but willingly; not for filthy lucre, but of a ready mind.* The diligent oversight Ignatius urges is Kepha’s willing, ungrudging shepherding (Ignatius to Polycarp 1:1).

1 Thessalonians 5:14 — *Now we exhort you, brethren, warn them that are unruly, comfort the feebleminded, support the weak, be patient toward all men.* The athlete who bears all maladies is the patient pastor supporting the weak (Ignatius to Polycarp 1:1).

Galatians 6:2 — *Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Messiah (Christ).* Ignatius’ “bear the maladies of all” is Sha’ul’s burden-bearing that fulfils—not abolishes—the law (Ignatius to Polycarp 1:1).

1 Peter 5:8 — *Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour.* The wisdom and watchfulness Ignatius commands answer the prowling adversary Kepha warns of (Ignatius to Polycarp 1:2).

Matthew 10:16 — *Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.* Ignatius is quoting the Messiah word-for-word—the serpent’s prudence and the dove’s guilelessness for the shepherd among wolves (Ignatius to Polycarp 1:2).

1 Peter 5:4 — *And when the chief Shepherd shall appear, ye shall receive a crown of glory that fadeth not away.* The athlete who is victorious through blows wins the unfading crown of the chief Shepherd (Ignatius to Polycarp 1:3).

2 Timothy 2:3 — *Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ).* Ignatius’ great athlete who receives blows and is victorious is the good soldier enduring hardness (Ignatius to Polycarp 1:3).

1 Corinthians 15:58 — *Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of Yahusha (Lord), forasmuch as ye know that your labour is not in vain in Yahusha (Lord).* The smitten anvil that stands firm is Sha’ul’s stedfast, unmoveable saint (Ignatius to Polycarp 1:3).

Ephesians 5:16 — *Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.* “Mark the seasons... await Him that is above every season” echoes the charge to redeem the time in evil days (Ignatius to Polycarp 1:3).

2 Timothy 2:8 — *Remember that Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) of the seed of David was raised from the dead according to my gospel.* The Eternal who became visible is the Messiah of David’s seed, truly in the flesh and truly raised (Ignatius to Polycarp 1:3).

1 Corinthians 15:3 — *For I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received, how that Messiah (Christ) died for our sins according to the scriptures.* Ignatius’ Impassible who suffered for our sake is the Messiah who truly died for sins (Ignatius to Polycarp 1:3).

Ephesians 5:2 — *And walk in love, as Messiah (Christ) also hath loved us, and hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to Elohim (God) for a sweetsmelling savour.* The sacrificial love that measures marriage is the Messiah’s self-offering (Ignatius to Polycarp 1:5).

Ephesians 5:25 — *Husbands, love your wives, even as Messiah (Christ) also loved the church, and gave himself for it.* Ignatius’ charge to love wives “as Yahuah loved the Church” is verbatim Sha’ul’s self-giving love (Ignatius to Polycarp 1:5).

Matthew 20:22 -- *But Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? They say unto him, We are able.* Polycarp's martyrdom "after the pattern of the Gospel" (Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:19) is the drinking of the cup the Master held out to His own.

1 Peter 1:11 -- *Searching what, or what manner of time the Spirit of Messiah (Christ) which was in them did signify, when it testified beforehand the sufferings of Messiah (Christ), and the glory that should follow.* The suffering-then-glory pattern Peter names is the very Gospel the martyrdom is said to be conformable to in Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:1.

Luke 23:34 -- *Then said Yahusha (Jesus), Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. And they parted his raiment, and cast lots.* The Master's own forbearance toward His executioners is the pattern of the witness Polycarp keeps in refusing to blaspheme his King (Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:9).

Acts 7:60 — *And he kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, Adonai (Lord), lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep.* Stephen the first martyr dies blessing his killers, the same constancy with which Polycarp faced his accusers (Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:8).

Romans 8:35 -- *Who shall separate us from the love of Messiah (Christ)? shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?* Neither the proconsul's threats nor the fire could separate Polycarp from the King he had served eighty-six years (Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:9).

Revelation 2:10 — *Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.* The Messiah spoke this to the church in Smyrna, Polycarp's own city, and Polycarp's "How then can I blaspheme my King who saved me?" (Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:9) is that faithfulness unto death.

Romans 8:17 — *And if children, then heirs; heirs of Elohim (God), and joint-heirs with Messiah (Christ); if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.* Polycarp, "a burnt sacrifice made ready and acceptable to Elohim (God)" (Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:14), is the suffering with Messiah that Paul says ends in being glorified together.

Daniel 12:2 -- *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.* Polycarp's hope of "resurrection of eternal life, both of soul and of body" (Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:14) rests on Daniel's promise of the awakening of the dead.

Matthew 20:23 -- *And he saith unto them, Ye shall drink indeed of my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with: but to sit on my right hand, and on my left, is not mine to give, but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared of my Father.* Polycarp's prayer to receive "a portion... in the cup of [Thy] Messiah" (Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:14) is the very cup the Master said His own would drink.

Malachi 3:3 — *And he shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver: and he shall purify the sons of Levi, and purge them as gold and silver, that they may offer unto Yahuah (LORD) an offering in righteousness.* Polycarp in the fire was "not like flesh burning, but like [a loaf in the oven or like] gold and silver refined in a furnace" (Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:15), the offering in righteousness the Refiner purges out.

Zechariah 13:9 -- *And I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried: they shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people: and they shall say, Yahuah (LORD) is my Elohim (God).* The refining of the faithful through fire is the same picture the witnesses saw in Polycarp's flame (Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:15).

1 Peter 1:7 -- *That the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire, might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ).* The body in the flame "like gold and silver refined in a furnace" (Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:15) is Peter's trial-by-fire of faith more precious than gold.

1 Peter 1:4 -- *To an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for you.* The Elohim "who maketh election from His own servants" (Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:20) keeps for His elect this incorruptible inheritance reserved in heaven.

Revelation 2:10 -- *Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.* Polycarp "crowned with the crown of immortality" (Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:17) receives the very crown of life promised to faithful Smyrna.

Psalms 116:15 -- *Precious in the sight of Yahuah (LORD) is the death of his saints.* The bones "more valuable than precious stones and finer than refined gold" (Martyrdom of Polycarp 1:18) are precious because the saint's death is precious to Yahuah Himself.

1 Corinthians 3:11 — *For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ).* The whole tower fits as one stone because it rests on the single foundation Sha'ul names (Hermas 3:2).

Luke 15:7 — *I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance.* The Lady's word that those who weep, if they repent, shall be glad, is heaven's own joy over the one sinner returning (Hermas 3:3).

Matthew 24:21 — *For then shall be great tribulation, such as was not since the beginning of the world to this time, no, nor ever shall be.* The Messiah names the very tribulation the beast of Hermas 4:2 is shown to typify.

Luke 15:7 — *I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance.* The Good Shepherd's joy over the recovered is the heart of the shepherd of repentance in Hermas 5:1.

2 Peter 3:9 — *Yahuah (Lord) is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.* The Master's longsuffering is why the angel of repentance is sent to dwell with Hermas in Hermas 5:1.

Ezekiel 18:30 — *Therefore I will judge you, O house of Yashar'el (Israel), every one according to his ways, saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD). Repent, and turn yourselves from all your transgressions; so iniquity shall not be your ruin.* The second repentance the shepherd offers in Hermas 9:3 is the prophet's call to turn and live.

Ezekiel 33:11 — *Say unto them, As I live, saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD), I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked; but that the wicked turn from his way and live: turn ye, turn ye from your evil ways; for why will ye die, O house of Yashar'el (Israel)?* The angel of repentance carries Yahuah's own ancient plea to the fallen in Hermas 5:1.

Psalm 15:2 — *He that walketh uprightly, and worketh righteousness, and speaketh the truth in his heart.* The pure heart that walks in the commandments in Hermas 5:1 is the dweller in Yahuah's holy hill.

Malachi 4:4 — *Remember ye the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Yashar'el (Israel), with the statutes and judgments.* The commandments Hermas is told to write and keep in Hermas 5:1 are the same statutes and judgments that endure.

1 John 5:3 — *For this is the love of Elohim (God), that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.* The keeping the shepherd commands in Hermas 5:1 is love made visible, the yoke that is not a burden.
John 14:15 — *If ye love me, keep my commandments.* The shepherd's call to keep and walk in the commandments with a pure heart in Hermas 5:1 is the Messiah's own measure of love.

Ezekiel 18:32 — *For I have no pleasure in the death of him that dieth, saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD): wherefore turn yourselves, and live ye.* The opposite that the unrepentant receive in Hermas 5:1 is the death Yahuah takes no pleasure in — turn, and live.

Matthew 7:14 — *Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.* The two outcomes the shepherd lays out in Hermas 5:1 are the two ways: the narrow road of keeping, or its opposite.

Revelation 2:5 — *Remember therefore from whence thou art fallen, and repent, and do the first works; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will remove thy candlestick out of his place, except thou repent.* The shepherd's either-or of promise or its opposite in Hermas 5:1 is the Messiah's own charge to repent and do the first works.

Deuteronomy 10:12 — *And now, Yashar'el (Israel), what doth Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) require of thee, but to fear Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) with all thy heart and with all thy soul,* Moses asks Yashar'el to fear, to walk in all His ways, to love and to serve; the Shepherd gives Hermas the same charge: "Believe Him therefore, and fear Him" (Hermas 6:1).

Matthew 19:9 — *And I say unto you, Whosoever shall put away his wife, except it be for fornication, and shall marry another, committeth adultery: and whoso marrieth her which is put away doth commit adultery.* The Shepherd's "Let him divorce her," and "if after divorcing his wife he shall marry another, he likewise committeth adultery" (Hermas 9:1) is the ruling Yahusha (Jesus) gave.

Matthew 19:17 — *And he said unto him, Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, Elohim (God): but if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments.* The Shepherd's "if thou keep my commandments and walk in them" (Hermas 9:2) is the road to life Yahusha (Jesus) gave: keep the commandments.

Ephesians 4:31 — *Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice:* the very catalogue of bitterness and wrath Hermas 10:2 says chokes the Spirit out of the vessel.

Proverbs 1:7 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.* The Shepherd calls the fear of Yahuah 'powerful and great and glorious' — Proverbs names it the very beginning of knowledge (Hermas 12:1).

Deuteronomy 10:12 — *And now, Yashar'el (Israel), what doth Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) require of thee, but to fear Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) with all thy heart and with all thy soul,* Moses' single requirement — fear and walk in His ways — is the soil from which the Shepherd's mandate grows (Hermas 12:1).

Psalm 111:10 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.* The Mandate's pairing of fear with commandment-keeping is the very wisdom of the Psalm, where to fear and to do are one (Hermas 12:1).

Ecclesiastes 12:13 — *Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear Elohim (God), and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.* Solomon's conclusion is the Shepherd's whole mandate — fear Yahuah and keep His commandments, the whole duty of man (Hermas 12:1).

1 John 5:3 — *For this is the love of Elohim (God), that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.* John defines the love the Shepherd commends — keeping commandments that are not grievous but life-giving (Hermas 12:1).

John 14:21 — *He that hath my commandments, and keepeth them, he it is that loveth me: and he that loveth me shall be loved of my Father, and I will love him, and will manifest myself to him.* Those who keep the commandments 'have life unto Elohim' in the Mandate because the Father loves and manifests Himself to the one who keeps them (Hermas 12:1).
John 14:15 — *If ye love me, keep my commandments.* The Messiah binds love to commandment-keeping exactly as the Shepherd binds life unto Elohim to keeping His commandments (Hermas 12:1).

Deuteronomy 10:20 — *Thou shalt fear Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God); him shalt thou serve, and to him shalt thou cleave, and swear by his name.* The Shepherd's "if thou fear Yahuah (Lord), thou shalt be master over the devil" (Hermas 12:1) rests on Moses' charge to fear and cleave to Yahuah alone.

Proverbs 8:13 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is to hate evil: pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, and the froward mouth, do I hate.* The Shepherd's "But fear thou the works of the devil, for they are evil" (Hermas 12:1) is the fear of Yahuah that Proverbs defines as the hatred of evil.

Matthew 10:28 — *And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.* The Messiah's ordering of fear — not the enemy but Yahuah alone — is exactly the Shepherd's 'fear not the devil... fear Yahuah' (Hermas 12:1).

Isaiah 1:16 — *Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil;* The Shepherd's "Be temperate as to what is evil, and do it not" (Hermas 13:1) is the prophet's call to cease to do evil, spoken to a people he would cleanse.

Isaiah 1:17 — *Learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.* The Shepherd's "to minister to widows, to visit the orphans and the needy" (Hermas 13:1) is the prophet's call to learn to do well.

James 1:7 — *For let not that man think that he shall receive any thing of Yahuah (Lord).* The Shepherd's "thou shalt surely receive none of thy petitions" (Hermas 14:1) for the one who wavers is Ya'aqov's (James's) own sentence on the man who doubts; it ain't new.

James 3:15 — *This wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish.* The Shepherd calls doubtful-mindedness "a daughter of the devil" and "an earthly spirit from the devil" (Hermas 14:1); Ya'aqov (James) gives the same verdict on what is earthly and devilish, not from above.

Mark 11:24 — *Therefore I say unto you, What things soever ye desire, when ye pray, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall have them.* The Shepherd's "they receive, because they ask without wavering, nothing doubting" (Hermas 14:1) is Yahusha's (Jesus') command to believe when you pray, that you may have; it ain't new.

Matthew 21:22 — *And all things, whatsoever ye shall ask in prayer, believing, ye shall receive.* The Shepherd's "thou shalt receive all things" (Hermas 14:1) for the one who asks nothing wavering is Yahusha's (Jesus') own word: ask in prayer, believing, and receive.

Hebrews 11:6 — *But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to Elohim (God) must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.* The Shepherd's "put on faith, for it is strong, and trust Elohim (God) that thou wilt receive all thy petitions which thou askest" (Hermas 14:1) rests on the same foundation: he that cometh to Elohim must believe He rewards the seeker.

Philippians 4:4 — *Rejoice in Yahusha (Lord) alway: and again I say, Rejoice.* The Shepherd's 'clothe thyself in cheerfulness... and rejoice in it' is Sha'ul's twice-spoken command to rejoice in Yahuah always (Hermas 15:3).

Deuteronomy 18:21 — *And if thou say in thine heart, How shall we know the word which Yahuah (LORD) hath not spoken?* Hermas asks, "shall a man know who of them is a prophet, and who a false prophet?" (Hermas 16:1), the very question Moses set before Yashar'el; it ain't new.

Jeremiah 23:16 — *Thus saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), Hearken not unto the words of the prophets that prophesy unto you: they make you vain: they speak a vision of their own heart, and not out of the mouth of Yahuah (LORD).* The Shepherd's empty prophet who answers out of his own emptiness is Jeremiah's prophet who speaks a vision of his own heart and not out of the mouth of Yahuah.

1 Peter 5:9 — *Whom resist stedfast in the faith, knowing that the same afflictions are accomplished in your brethren that are in the world.* The Shepherd's "having armed thyself with the fear of Yahuah (Lord), resist them" (Hermas 17:2) is Kepha's (Peter's) charge to resist, stedfast in the faith.

1 Peter 5:9 — *Whom resist stedfast in the faith, knowing that the same afflictions are accomplished in your brethren that are in the world.* The angel's "If then ye resist him, he will be vanquished" (Hermas 17:5) is Kepha's (Peter's) charge to resist, stedfast in the faith.

James 4:7 — *Submit yourselves therefore to Elohim (God). Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.* The angel of repentance's "Fear him not therefore; and he will flee from you" (Hermas 17:4) is Ya'aqov's (James's) word: resist the devil and he will flee.

1 Timothy 6:8 — *And having food and raiment let us be therewith content.* The "a competency which is sufficient for thee" that Hermas commands the sojourner to prepare (Hermas 18:1) is Sha'ul's own contentment with food and raiment.

Isaiah 58:6 — *Is not this the fast that I have chosen? to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, and to let the oppressed go free, and that ye break every yoke?* The Shepherd's "do no wickedness in thy life… observe His commandments and walk in His ordinances" (Hermas 22:1) is the prophet's own fast that looses wickedness.

Matthew 7:21 — *Not every one that saith unto me, Adonai (Lord), Adonai (Lord), shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.* The factious and lawless who say but do not keep are the Master's own who cry Lord, Lord yet do not do the Father's will — saying is not the doing.
